## Reproducible Data Science

### The Importance of Reproducible Research: Main Steps

Here, you should explain why research needs to be reproducible and transparent, and provide a brief overview of the key steps involved.

### Open Science and FAIR Data Principles

Summarise the main principles of Open Science and explain what FAIR Data Principles stand for. Explain the main steps one should take to make their work reproducible.

### Resources and Platforms 

To make research more reproducible, researchers can use a variety of digital tools and platforms throughout the research workflow.

- **[GitHub](https://github.com?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**: GitHub supports version control and collaboration. It allows researchers to track changes in their code, work in branches, and share their projects with others.

- **[Posit (RStudio)](https://posit.co?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**: Posit provides an integrated development environment for R. It helps researchers write scripts, create R Markdown documents, and organise their analyses.

- **[CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**: CRAN is the main repository for R packages. Researchers can install and manage packages needed for data analysis.

- **[Open Science Framework (OSF)](https://osf.io?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**: OSF allows researchers to share datasets, protocols, and project materials in an open and transparent way.

- **[Zenodo](https://zenodo.org?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**: Zenodo enables researchers to archive datasets, code, and publications, and provides a DOI for citation.

Using these platforms helps researchers document their workflow, share materials openly, and ensure that analyses can be reproduced by others.
